Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{QP}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{RS}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{RT}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{RP}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{QS}$ in terms of $a,b,c,$ and $d.$
worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $S$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$ 

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QS}=\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PR}+\overset{\to }{RS}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/317d78cec35bc3721ebbd64ac1ed53aa5b36c89101a170b93805d17c670f2673.png)

  

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QP}=a,\,\overset{\to }{PR}=-d,\,\overset{\to }{RT}=b.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/ff4b4292bb8a15551cb22da1f621684e9fdf24d35ae873b408dc612e5b3255e8.png)

   

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QS} & =\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PR}+\overset{\to }{RS} \\  & =a-d+b.\end{aligned}
$$
